Part of the Perch papers: the Perch paper · its simulation section · Perch and oz-policy-builder · all Perch documents

Dual simulation · runs offline in this page

OpenZeppelin and Perch, side by side in soroban-sim

One payment rule for an app key is installed on two smart accounts: an OpenZeppelin v0.8.0 account whose rule carries an oz-policy-builder predicate and OpenZeppelin's spending_limit, and a Perch account with one grant. You build the requests. Each one runs against both accounts' contract WebAssembly on a local Soroban host in this tab, and both authorization traces and verdicts appear side by side.

The rule: the app key may move XLM out of the account with transfer on the native asset contract, only to the shop. On the OZ account, the interpreter's predicate pins the recipient and bounds each transfer at 10 XLM, and spending_limit adds a total of 10 XLM per 100 ledgers OPB policy-synth/README.md:400-402. On the Perch account, the shop grant (grant ID 1) pins the recipient and caps the total at 10 XLM per 100 ledgers rule-core cap.rs:169-205. The owner installs both.

Simulation by soroban-sim (theahaco/soroban-sim d029384, soroban-env-host 29.0.2), compiled to WebAssembly and run in a worker: no wallet, no RPC, no network request. Keys are throwaway Ed25519 keys. Every verdict, code, trace, balance and hash on this page comes from that run; the page itself only counts replies and marks which recorded spends still fall inside the 100-ledger window. The notes beside them cite source lines (hover a grey tag for the full path).

Build a scenario

Not started. Starting compiles a 3.5 MB WebAssembly module in a worker in this tab, then sets up both ledgers and installs the rule.

Each request card says whether its reply, minus timings, has the same SHA-256 as the recorded native run. The full page shows the reference run and every contract's Wasm hash.

Every request goes to both accounts. The spending_limit switch changes only the OZ rule, through the account's own remove_policy and add_policy, authorized by the owner through rule 0 OZ smart_account/mod.rs:523-526 OZ smart_account/mod.rs:490-493; the predicate stays as policy-synth produced it. Perch's window is part of the shop grant, so the switch sends nothing to the Perch account. Refused requests run as an enforcing simulation of the signed transaction and are never submitted; allowed ones are submitted and applied, one ledger each.

"Run the reference scenario" resets both ledgers and sends them here; each reply, minus wall-clock timings, is hashed and compared with the native record. What soroban-sim makes visible

  • The contracts' own bytes run. Both accounts, the interpreter, spending_limit and Perch's verifier and compiler execute as WebAssembly built from the pinned sources; the table below says which bytes match a deployment and which do not. The three OpenZeppelin-side contracts equal oz-policy-builder's testnet records; the Perch account is built from f0275f4 and is not deployed. Nothing in either design is mocked.
  • Offline and deterministic. One Soroban host (soroban-env-host 29.0.2) runs in a worker in this tab, on ledgers forked from recorded protocol-29 network settings. A fixed scenario returns the same replies on every run.
  • The same replies natively, under WASI and here. One Rust driver over soroban-sim runs natively, as a wasm32-wasip1 reactor in Node, and as this page's reactor. The reference scenario's replies agree in all three, except wall-clock time; each request card above says whether this browser's reply matches the native one.
  • Inspectable authorization. Each trace row is a diagnostic event the host emitted: which contract ran which function, at what depth, and which error stopped it. Each card shows the authorization entries that were signed, and for a refusal, that the fingerprint of every ledger entry the session wrote is unchanged.
  • Two designs, one host. The OZ and Perch accounts run on separate ledgers forked from the same settings and receive the same requests. The columns differ by the account design and by the signer kind each accepts: on the OZ side the app is a delegated Stellar account whose signature the host checks, in an authorization entry of its own; on the Perch side it is an Ed25519 key that a verifier contract checks, inside the account's one entry. Each ledger closes only its own transactions, so after an OZ-only change their ledger numbers differ.

What runs here, and what does not

  • Executed. The contracts' WebAssembly; the Soroban host's authorization (tree matching, nonces, expiry, classic account signatures, __check_auth, policy calls); soroban-sim's transaction validation and application for every allowed request and every owner change.
  • Simulator substitutions. Each account has its own local ledger, forked from protocol-29 network settings recorded from testnet ledger 5,301,502 (soroban-env-host 29.0.2 at protocol 29; testnet has since moved to protocol 30), with the passphrase Standalone Network ; February 2017. A throwaway fee payer is funded in the fork; the shop and the other recipient are funded by override, and on the OZ side so are the owner, the app key and the stranger, which sign as classic accounts; Perch's compiler and verifier are placed at the addresses its build pins derive. One transaction closes one ledger.
  • Refusals are enforcing simulations. A refused request is not submitted, so this page makes no claim about the fee a failed, submitted transaction would pay. A transfer the account cannot fund fails in the recording simulation and is reported as failed, with nothing signed.
  • Not shown. Passkey signers, OpenZeppelin threshold policies, rule expiry, signer rotation, revocation, Perch recovery and grant generations, and contract upgrades.
